summary: Describes what SCTP is good for, compares it with TCP and UDP, and gives guidelines on when to use it and when not to. It is informational.

eli5.summary: SCTP is another way to send data. This explains when it beats the two common ways and when it does not.

subtitle: When SCTP is a better fit than TCP or UDP, and when it is not.

tldr.problem: Implementers and protocol designers need guidance on whether to pick SCTP, TCP, RTP or UDP, since the protocols overlap in what they offer.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC compares the service models of TCP, SCTP and UDP, then covers SCTP multihoming, NAT handling and security.
tldr.outcome: SCTP provides everything TCP does plus multi-streams, multihoming, message boundaries and unordered reliable delivery; it was not yet widely deployed when written.

today: RFC 3257 is an Informational document and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It describes SCTP as defined in RFC 2960, and notes SCTP was not yet widely deployed when it was written.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
SCTP is a reliable transport protocol (RFC 2960) that, together with TCP, RTP and UDP, provides transport-layer services to upper layers. All four are IETF standards-track transport protocols, each with its own domain of applicability and some overlap.

This document guides implementers and protocol designers in choosing among them, with special attention to the services that would make SCTP the right choice. An association is an SCTP connection between two endpoints, and a transport address is an IP address plus an SCTP port number.
sections.eli5: There are several ways to send data over the Internet. This note helps you pick the right one for the job.

sections.title: Comparing TCP, SCTP and UDP
sections.content:
TCP is connection-oriented: it needs a connection set up before data and a tear-down afterwards. It offers data reliability, sequence preservation, and flow and congestion control.

SCTP is also connection-oriented and provides all of those services, so many applications will find either one meets their needs. SCTP may cost more to process than TCP when it runs with a single ordered stream and one address pair. It adds four capabilities: multiple independent streams in one association (easing head-of-line blocking), multihoming with transparent failover, preservation of message boundaries, and unordered reliable delivery.

UDP is connectionless and gives only best-effort delivery and preserved message boundaries. Applications that do not need reliable transfer of more than a packet's worth of data, including some transaction-based ones, will find it adequate.
sections.eli5: TCP is a phone call where words arrive in order. UDP is a postcard. SCTP is a phone call that can carry several conversations at once and has a backup line.

sections.title: Multihoming
sections.content:
SCTP supports multihoming at the transport layer, which can add robustness against network failures. The RFC cites signaling transport of PSTN signaling messages as an example where this is important.

It covers only communication between two endpoints that have multiple IP addresses, not clustered endpoints that switch to another endpoint on failure. For truly fault-resilient communication each endpoint needs more than one network interface. The number of paths used is the minimum of the interfaces used by either endpoint.

Source address choice matters: always using the same source address can leave a single point of failure. An endpoint should pick the source address matching the interface the packet leaves from, but must never use one that is not part of the association (the binding address constraint).
sections.eli5: Having two roads between two houses means that if one road is closed, the mail still gets through.

sections.title: SCTP and NAT
sections.content:
If an endpoint is behind a network address translator (NAT), the RFC gives two options. The first is for single-homed sessions: send no transport addresses in the INIT or INIT ACK chunk, so the peer uses the IP header source address. Any multihoming behind the NAT is then invisible to the peer.

For multihoming through a NAT, the NAT needs a public address for each internal address. The host can preconfigure an address for the NAT to substitute, or the NAT can use an application layer gateway to translate addresses in the INIT and INIT ACK chunks. With port translation on a multihomed endpoint, translation must apply per association so the endpoint sees the same port number for all messages in it.

The second option is to use the hostname feature and DNS, with the hostname in the INIT or INIT ACK and resolved before the association is fully set up. RFC 2694 covers NAT and DNS issues.
sections.eli5: A NAT is like a receptionist who rewrites the return address on letters. SCTP can either let the receptionist handle one address, or give names instead of numbers.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
TCP can suffer blind denial of service attacks that flood a host with SYN packets until its SYN-queue fills. SYN cookies reduce the risk, though window scale cannot then be used. The RFC says forging a connection against current SYN-cookie implementations is on the order of 1 in 2^24.

SCTP was designed with that experience in mind. Each side uses a 32-bit Verification Tag so a datagram can be checked as belonging to the association. A cookie is mandatory in association setup: after INIT, INIT-ACK and COOKIE-ECHO, the server has fully established it. The cookie carries an HMAC (MD5 or SHA-1) over the cookie and a server secret key, and resources are reserved only for a valid COOKIE-ECHO. Blind forgery is lower than 1 in 2^128.

SCTP increases availability only and has no mechanism for message authentication, integrity or confidentiality; it relies on IPsec or the application protocol. TLS over SCTP must always use in-order streams. With IPsec, one endpoint with N addresses and another with M needs 2 * N * M security associations. Neither TCP nor SCTP protects against man-in-the-middle session hijacking, and the secret key should follow RFC 1750. SCTP was not yet widely deployed, so new issues could emerge.
sections.eli5: SCTP asks for a secret handshake with a signed ticket before it saves a seat, so pranksters sending fake requests have a much harder time.
